frequency_question: How often do structural and procedural interventions successfully prevent or delay the implementation of announced major unilateral tariffs?
membership_rule: Includes sweeping unilateral tariff announcements by U.S. presidents intended to take effect within a short window, where institutional friction (litigation, mandatory administrative notice-and-comment periods, statutory interagency review processes) is actively mobilized.

cases.name: Trump Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs

coverage_note: 6 major instances identified representing primary post-ERISA/Trade Act unilateral tariff episodes.
known_gaps: Minor sectoral tariff adjustments excluded; focuses on sweeping macroeconomic threats.
skeleton: Total major unilateral tariff threats with immediate implementation timelines vs. those successfully blocked or delayed by institutional/structural friction before taking effect.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 6 major historical instances
validity_reason: Statutory authorities governing trade (Trade Act of 1974, Section 232, International Emergency Economic Powers Act) remain stable across administrations.
